extracted.intended_audience: parties/participants and counsel in NRC adjudicatory proceedings (license transfer and related hearings), presiding officers, and NRC staff
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and evidentiary rules governing notice, submissions, scheduling, presiding officer powers, hearings (oral and written), initial decisions, stays, and NRC staff participation in adjudications on license transfer and related matters under 10 CFR subparts M and N.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on party-to-party discovery
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as otherwise permitted by subpart C, a party may not seek discovery from any other party or the NRC or its personnel, whether by document production, deposition, interrogatories or otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a broad restriction on discovery in proceedings under this subpart; any permitted discovery must come from subpart C.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motions and requests general requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for motions and requests and responses in proceedings under this subpart are as specified in § 2.323.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties must follow the filing, service, and procedural requirements that § 2.323 sets out (refer to that section for format, service, timing, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-examination motion and cross-examination plan content
rubrics_metrics.description: A party seeking to permit party cross-examination must file a motion accompanied by a cross-examination plan containing: (i) brief description of the issue(s) to be cross-examined; (ii) the objective to be achieved; and (iii) the proposed line of questions that may logically lead to achieving that objective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The plan is required with the motion and must identify the issue, objective, and proposed line of questioning to justify party cross-examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality and handling of cross-examination plans and proposed questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Cross-examination plans and proposed questions submitted to the presiding officer must be kept in confidence by the presiding officer until issuance of the initial decision; upon issuance they shall be provided to the Commission's Secretary for inclusion in the official record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties submit these materials only to the presiding officer; they are confidential during adjudication and become part of the official record after the initial decision is issued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard for allowing party cross-examination
rubrics_metrics.description: The presiding officer shall allow cross-examination by the parties only if the presiding officer determines that such cross-examination is necessary to ensure the development of an adequate record for decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permission for party cross-examination is discretionary and contingent on necessity to develop an adequate record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and content requirements for motions for summary disposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Motions for summary disposition must be submitted no later than 45 days before the commencement of hearing unless directed otherwise, be in writing, include a written explanation of the basis, and attach a short and concise statement of material facts the moving party contends there is no genuine issue to be heard; must be served on parties and the Secretary when submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other parties may answer within 20 days; the presiding officer must issue a determination no later than 15 days before hearing and apply the standards in subpart G.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral vs. written hearing default
rubrics_metrics.description: Hearings under this subpart will be oral hearings unless, within 15 days of service of the order granting the request for hearing, the parties unanimously agree and file a joint motion requesting a hearing consisting of written submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A written-only hearing requires unanimous consent; otherwise, the default is an oral hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted submissions in an oral hearing (initial and responsive materials)
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants in an oral hearing may submit initial written statements of position and written testimony with supporting affidavits on admitted contentions, and written responses and rebuttal testimony with supporting affidavits directed to initial materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial materials must be filed on dates set by the presiding officer; responses/rebuttals generally must be filed within 20 days of service of initial materials unless the presiding officer directs otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed questions for the presiding officer — deadlines and filing
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties may submit proposed questions for the presiding officer to consider propounding to sponsors of testimony: (i) general proposed questions due no later than 20 days after service of initial materials (or 5 days before hearing if that 20-day date is <5 days before hearing); (ii) proposed questions to rebuttal due within 7 days after service of rebuttal (or 5 days before hearing if that date is <5 days). Proposed questions need not be filed with other parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The presiding officer may propound at discretion; deadlines are truncated close to hearing; proposed questions are submitted only to the presiding officer and kept confidential until propounded or initial decision is issued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of proposed questions — discretion and record inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions submitted may be propounded at the presiding officer's discretion and must be kept confidential until propounded or until the initial decision; afterward, the presiding officer provides them to the Commission's Secretary for the official record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presiding officer controls whether proposed questions are used; confidentiality rules apply as with cross-examination plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral hearing procedural requirements (transcript, evidence form, witnesses)
rubrics_metrics.description: Oral hearings must be transcribed; written testimony is received into evidence in exhibit form; participants may designate and present their own witnesses; NRC staff testimony will be presented only by persons designated by the Executive Director for Operations or delegee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are mandatory procedural elements for oral hearings; the record is created by transcript and exhibits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Questioning in oral hearings — who may question
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants and witnesses will be questioned orally or in writing only by the presiding officer or the presiding officer's designee. The presiding officer will use questions prepared by the presiding officer/designee, questions submitted by participants at the presiding officer's discretion, or a combination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties do not directly question witnesses; the presiding officer controls questioning and may address individuals or panels. Parties generally may not submit proposed questions at the hearing except upon the presiding officer's request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability and scheduling rules for hearings consisting of written presentations
rubrics_metrics.description: In hearings consisting of written presentations, participants may submit initial written statements/testimony, written responses and rebuttal (with supporting affidavits) within 20 days, written questions on responses/rebuttal within 7 days, and written concluding statements within 20 days of service of responses or rebuttals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The presiding officer may formulate and submit written questions to develop an adequate record; deadlines mirror oral hearing timelines but are tailored for written-only proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-hearing proposed findings and format
rubrics_metrics.description: Each party must file written post-hearing proposed findings of fact and conclusions of law within 30 days of the close of the hearing (or other time as directed), and these must conform to the format requirements in § 2.712(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timeliness and format requirements are mandatory for post-hearing submissions of findings and conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial decision requirements and effect
rubrics_metrics.description: The presiding officer shall render an initial decision after completion of an informal hearing unless the Commission directs otherwise. The initial decision constitutes the final action of the Commission 120 days after issuance unless a party petitions for Commission review, the Commission directs review for inconsistency with staff action, or the Commission takes sua sponte review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial decisions must be in writing, based only on the record or officially noticed facts, and must include findings/conclusions on all material issues, the ruling/order and effective date, actions NRC staff shall take if inconsistent with staff action, and timing for petitions and finality; pending review the initial decision resolving all issues is immediately effective unless otherwise provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on seeking judicial review before Commission review
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise authorized by law, a party must file a petition for Commission review before seeking judicial review of an agency action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow § 2.341 procedures for petitions for Commission review as prerequisite to judicial review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application for stay — timing and page limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications for a stay of the effectiveness of the NRC staff's action in a hearing under this subpart must be filed with the presiding officer within seven (7) days of issuance of the notice of the NRC staff's action, and must be no longer than ten (10) pages exclusive of affidavits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short page-limited filings; answers may be filed within ten (10) days; further replies are not entertained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application for stay — content required
rubrics_metrics.description: A stay application must contain a concise summary of the action requested to be stayed and a concise statement of the grounds for a stay, with reference to the factors specified (irreparable injury, likelihood to prevail on merits, harm to others, public interest).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should explicitly address the stay factors in their concise statement; answers should concisely address these matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stay factors to be considered
rubrics_metrics.description: In determining whether to grant or deny a stay, the presiding officer/Commission will consider: (1) whether the requestor will be irreparably injured unless a stay is granted; (2) whether the requestor has made a strong showing it is likely to prevail on the merits; (3) whether granting the stay would harm other participants; and (4) where the public interest lies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the four enumerated balancing factors for stay decisions; applicants should address each.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subpart M scope — when this subpart governs
rubrics_metrics.description: Subpart M governs all adjudicatory proceedings on applications for direct or indirect transfer of control of an NRC license when the transfer requires prior NRC approval; it provides the only mechanism for requesting hearings on license transfer requests unless contrary case-specific orders are issued by the Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Subpart M procedures for license transfer hearings unless the Commission orders otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public notice of receipt of license transfer applications
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission will place a copy of each transfer application on the NRC website and will publish Federal Register notices of receipt for transfers involving parts 50, 52, and 53 licenses, major fuel cycle facility licenses under part 70, or part 72 licenses; these notices constitute the § 2.105 notice for matters requiring NRC approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public availability is through the website and FR publication for certain license classes; periodic lists can be requested from the Public Document Room.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of application-related documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless exempt under part 9, the license transfer application and associated requests, Commission correspondence with applicant/licensee, Federal Register notices, the NRC staff Safety Evaluation Report (SER), any NRC staff order acting on the application, and if a hearing is held, the hearing record and decision will be placed on the NRC website when available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document availability is subject to part 9 exemptions; the SER and hearing record are specifically listed for posting when available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written comments as alternative to hearings — status and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons may submit written comments regarding license transfer applications as an alternative to requests for hearings and petitions to intervene; the Commission will consider and may respond, but such comments do not become part of the decisional record. Comments should be submitted within 30 days after public notice and addressed to the Secretary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The applicant receives a copy and may respond within 10 days; applicant responses likewise do not constitute part of the decisional record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice content for oral hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: A notice of oral hearing must state the time, place, and issues to be considered; provide names and addresses of participants; specify the time limit for indicating intent to present views; specify schedules for filings (testimony, positions, proposed questions, rebuttal) consistent with § 2.1321; specify that oral hearing shall commence within 15 days of the date for submittal of rebuttal testimony unless ordered otherwise; state other appropriate instructions; and, if so determined, direct that staff participate as a party for some or all issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the Commission is not the Presiding Officer, additional items about Presiding Officer jurisdiction, powers, and instructions to certify the record promptly must be included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice content for hearing consisting of written comments
rubrics_metrics.description: A notice for a written-comments hearing must state the issues to be considered; provide names and addresses of participants; specify schedules for filing written testimony, statements of position, proposed questions for the Presiding Officer to consider, and rebuttal consistent with § 2.1321; and state other instructions the Commission deems appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Schedules and procedural instructions mirror oral hearings but are targeted to written-submission format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions in notices/orders — restricting testimony and representation
rubrics_metrics.description: A notice or order granting a hearing shall restrict irrelevant or duplicative testimony and require common interests to be represented by a single participant. If a participant's interests do not extend to all issues, the notice or order may limit that participant's participation accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The intent is to avoid redundancy and ensure efficient representation of common interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generic determination on administrative license amendments reflecting transfers
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise determined, amendments that merely conform the license to reflect the transfer are determined to involve 'no significant hazards consideration' or 'no genuine issue' as to public health and safety being significantly affected; administrative amendments to reflect an approved transfer will be included in the transfer order and challenges limited to whether the amendment accurately reflects the approved transfer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Challenges to such administrative amendments are narrowly confined to accuracy in reflecting the approved transfer.

rubrics_metrics.name: NRC staff authority and participation role in Subpart M proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: During pendency of a hearing, consistent with staff findings in its SER, the staff is expected to promptly issue approval or denial of transfer requests and notify the Presiding Officer and parties; the staff is not required to be a party but will offer its SER and provide sponsoring witness(es). Within 15 days of issuance of the order admitting contentions, the staff must notify whether it desires to participate as a party, identify contentions it wishes to participate on, and make required disclosures (or provide an affidavit explaining why disclosures cannot be provided). Once it chooses to participate, the staff has all rights and responsibilities of a party for the contentions it joins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staff actions and choice to participate have procedural consequences; staff disclosure obligations apply unless explained by affidavit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presiding Officer designation, disqualification, and replacement procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission will ordinarily be the Presiding Officer, but the notice may state otherwise. Participants may move for disqualification with an affidavit stating grounds. If not granted and the presiding person is not the Commission, the Commission will decide. A presiding person who is disqualified shall withdraw on the record; if a Presiding Officer becomes unavailable the Commission will designate a replacement. Motions concerning designation of a replacement must be made within 5 days after designation. Unless ordered otherwise, the jurisdiction of a Presiding Officer other than the Commission commences as designated and terminates on certification of the record to the Commission or upon disqualification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural time limits and affidavit requirements control disqualification practice; Commission is ultimate decisionmaker if dispute arises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presiding Officer powers and responsibilities in oral hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: The Presiding Officer shall conduct a fair hearing, develop a record for informed decisionmaking, and within the Commission's framework have powers to avoid unnecessary delay and maintain order; dispose of procedural requests; question participants and witnesses and entertain suggested questions; order consolidation of participants; establish order of presentation; hold conferences; establish time limits; limit number of witnesses; and strike or reject duplicative, unreliable, immaterial, or irrelevant presentations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These enumerated powers are broad and intended to facilitate orderly, efficient hearings and sound record development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presiding Officer actions when Commission does not preside
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Commission does not preside, the Presiding Officer may certify questions or refer rulings to the Commission, any hearing order may be modified by the Commission, and the Presiding Officer will certify the completed hearing record to the Commission which may issue decision or direct additional testimony.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presiding Officer's actions are subject to Commission review and modification; certification of the record triggers Commission action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participation and schedule for written-comments hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants in written-comments hearings may submit initial written positions/testimony (date set by Commission or Presiding Officer), written responses/rebuttal and proposed written questions within 20 days of initial filings, written questions on rebuttal within 7 days, and written concluding statements within 20 days of service of responses (unless directed otherwise).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deadlines reflect a predictable written-exchange schedule; presiding officer or Commission may alter timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participation and schedule for oral hearings (detailed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants may submit initial written positions/testimony, written responses/rebuttal and proposed questions within 20 days of initial filings, proposed questions to rebuttal within 7 days, and the oral hearing should commence within 65 days of the Commission's notice granting a hearing unless directed otherwise. Questioning is ordinarily conducted by the Presiding Officer. Written post-hearing statements may be submitted within 20 days of close of oral hearing. Commission may use additional procedures or convene a formal hearing under subpart G for specific substantial disputes of fact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard timeline is 65 days to commencement; timing of exchanges is regimented; Commission may escalate to formal hearing procedures where necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation of testimony in oral hearing — filing deadlines and form
rubrics_metrics.description: All direct testimony in an oral hearing must be filed no later than 15 days before the hearing (or as ordered); written testimony will be received into evidence in exhibit form; participants may designate/present their own witnesses; NRC staff testimony only by designated staff persons; participants and witnesses will be questioned only by the Presiding Officer; the Presiding Officer may accept written testimony from a person unable to appear and may request written responses to questions; subpoenas will not be granted at the request of participants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict pre-hearing filing deadline for direct testimony; limitations on subpoenas and who presents staff testimony; Presiding Officer controls accommodation for absent witnesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appearance, representation, and exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: A participant may appear on their own behalf or be represented by an authorized representative; persons appearing must file a written notice stating name, address, telephone number and basis of eligibility if representing someone; persons may be excluded for disorderly, dilatory or contemptuous conduct provided they are informed of grounds and given an opportunity to respond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal notice requirements for representation and procedural due process before excluding participants for misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motions and requests filings and response times
rubrics_metrics.description: Motions and requests shall be addressed to the Presiding Officer and, if written, filed with the Secretary and served on other participants; responses to written motions shall be filed within 5 days after service unless directed otherwise; the Presiding Officer may entertain motions for extension of time and schedule changes; when Commission does not preside the Presiding Officer may refer rulings or certify questions to the Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prompt service and short response periods are standard; motions and referrals do not stay or extend aspect of hearing unless ordered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application for stay of NRC staff action on license transfer — special timing
rubrics_metrics.description: An application for a stay of the NRC staff's order on a license transfer must be filed with the Commission within 5 days of issuance of the notice of staff action, must be no longer than 10 pages exclusive of affidavits, must include a concise summary and grounds for stay with reference to stay factors, and answers must be filed within 10 days; the Commission will consider irreparable injury, likelihood to prevail, harm to others, and public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a distinct and expedited stay process for staff orders on license transfers with tight deadlines and page limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission action after hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon completion of a hearing the Commission will issue a written opinion including its decision on the license transfer application and reasons; decisions on issues designated for hearing under § 2.309 will be based on the record developed at hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commission decisions must be reasoned and grounded on the hearing record for designated issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subpart N purpose, sunset, and review requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Subpart N provides simplified procedures for expedited resolution of disputes with oral hearings; it shall cease to have effect on January 8, 2027 unless extended for not more than 5 years after the NRC offers the public an opportunity to provide input on costs and benefits and considers that input; the NRC will publish a Federal Register document announcing its determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subpart N is temporary and subject to public input before any extension; users must be aware of the sunset date and potential revision process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expedited proceedings — prohibition of written pleadings and briefs
rubrics_metrics.description: For proceedings under Subpart N, except where provided otherwise or requested by the presiding officer, written pleadings and briefs are not permitted (regardless of form).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The expedited process emphasizes oral argument and limits written submissions, subject to narrow exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expedited proceedings — oral motions and limitations on dispositive motions
rubrics_metrics.description: All motions must be presented and argued orally; motions for summary disposition before the hearing has concluded and motions for reconsideration to the presiding officer or Commission are not permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties should prepare to make and argue motions orally; the expedited track restricts pre-hearing dispositive motions and reconsideration requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expedited proceedings — rulings recorded and no discovery
rubrics_metrics.description: The presiding officer will reflect rulings on motions and other requests in a written decision or a verbatim transcript; except for information disclosure requirements in subpart C, requests for discovery will not be entertained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rulings must be captured in a written decision or transcript; general discovery is unavailable in the expedited track.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expedited proceedings — presiding officer orders and transfer to other subparts
rubrics_metrics.description: The presiding officer may issue written orders and rulings necessary for orderly conduct; if a proceeding is inappropriate for Subpart N, the presiding officer or Commission may order continuation under another subpart, and if discontinued, the presiding officer may issue written orders for orderly continuation under another subpart.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flexibility exists to move proceedings out of the expedited track if inappropriate; the presiding officer manages transition sequencing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expedited proceedings — cross-examination request procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: A party may present an oral motion to permit party cross-examination on particular admitted contentions or issues; the presiding officer may allow party cross-examination if necessary for development of an adequate record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even in expedited proceedings, party cross-examination is allowed only by oral motion and upon a necessity finding by the presiding officer.

rubrics_metrics.name: NRC staff role in expedited proceedings — notification content
rubrics_metrics.description: During pendency of any hearing under Subpart N, consistent with staff findings in its review and as authorized by law, the NRC staff is expected to promptly issue approval or denial of the application or take other appropriate action and must notify the presiding officer and parties; that notice must include the NRC staff's explanation why public health and safety is protected and why the action accords with common defense and security despite the pendency of the contested matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staff notifications in expedited proceedings must include substantive explanation addressing public health/safety and common defense/security to justify action during pendency.
